scope: Actual NTK PDF.js extraction and pixels. Differential engine/SQLite/MCP tests against pre-optimization installed source, in an isolated profile/store. Does not test actual ChatGPT generation or public tunnel behavior.

checks.name: ordinary search results stay identical; exact statement queries prefer actual statements
every paragraph preserves UTF-16 ranges, Unicode/math, clipping and expansion cursors
prepared statements and result cache preserve SQL binding/null/BigInt/truncation semantics
quality heuristic matches old engine on all NTK pages and damaged/Unicode boundary cases
SQL errors do not poison later calls; forbidden access remains denied
combined search/read matches separate search plus read, source and budget exactly
concurrent cache hits keep independent response objects and snapshot source
forced idle eviction, timeout and recovery preserve search correctness
Figure 3 overview/crop/zoom pixels, duplicate reference and resend are unchanged
real MCP schema forwards merged reads without duplicating source in text envelopes
heading-only fast reads warn explicitly and provide a working content-expansion call
cached NTK SQL cannot bypass text budgets and reference-only reads remain available
restart restores the same NTK share, references and encrypted source/image history
revocation blocks even warm cached queries and does not modify the original PDF

tradeoffs: The first uncached search pays index construction after lazy registration.
SQL worker retention is 5 minutes instead of 30 seconds; memory can stay resident longer. Cache size remains bounded.
A first search hit is not guaranteed relevant or complete: its exact text and clipping/cursors are preserved.
Model answer quality/latency and actual ChatGPT compaction are outside these engine checks.

findings.risk: A short high-ranked appendix cross-reference can be read before the requested statement; this is a retrieval sufficiency risk, not a measured ChatGPT hallucination.
findings.resolution: Exact numbered-statement queries prefer actual statements while preserving explicit page scopes and proof-specific queries.

findings.risk: paragraphComplete=true can still mean only a section heading was read.
findings.resolution: Heading assessment, explicit MCP warning, and an executable next-paragraph expansion; preserved after source recovery.

initialHarnessCorrection: The initial concurrent-result assertion compared bounded SQL text to an unbounded page. Both engines already clip individual cells at 3,000 characters; the expectation was corrected and all comparisons passed.
